result.stdout:
Usage: mksecret [options]

Generate a random secret. Default mode: a random-character password. Subcommands: phrase, key.

Options:
  --quiet                      Suppress the stderr entropy note.
  -n, --count N                Number of secrets to emit, one per line. Default 1 (max 100000).
  -l, --length N               Password length in characters. Default 20 (max 4096).
  -c, --charset NAME           Character set: alphanumeric (default), full, alpha, digits, safe.
  -h, --help                   Show help
  --version                    Show version
  --no-color                   Disable colored output
  --json                       JSON output
  --describe                   Structured JSON metadata for AI agents
  --color[=auto|always|never]  Coloured output: auto (default when omitted), always, or never

Subcommands:
  mksecret password [--length N] [--charset NAME]   (default)
  mksecret phrase   [--words N] [--sep S] [--capitalize] [--number]
  mksecret key      [--bytes N] [--encoding hex|base64|base64url|base32]

  Run 'mksecret SUBCOMMAND --help' for mode-specific flags.

Examples:
  mksecret                             20-char alphanumeric password
  mksecret --length 32 --charset full  32 chars including symbols
  mksecret --charset safe              Avoids visually-ambiguous characters
  mksecret --count 5                   Five passwords, one per line

Composes with:
  mksecret | clip  Copy a generated password to the clipboard without it touching the terminal

Exit Codes:
  0    Success (a closed downstream pipe, e.g. | head -1, also exits 0 — not an error)
  125  Usage error: unknown flag, bad --charset/--encoding value, non-positive or oversized --length/--bytes/--words/--count, unexpected positional (including an unrecognised subcommand)
  126  Runtime error: OS CSPRNG failure or output write failure (disk full, device error)
